Design decisions worth carrying forward:
- Mixin does NOT inherit IComponent (avoids duplicate/virtual base); reaches GetEntityId/GetSimContext via CRTP.
- Exposes no entt::registry accessor, and Get<T>() static_asserts T is one of the component's own declared storage structs - ADR Decision 5 enforced by construction, not convention.
- DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR needs NO analogue: plain 'new CCmpX()' already gives the address-stable, individually-heap-allocated proxy Decision 3 requires. Reasoning recorded in ADR Appendix A so it isn't re-litigated.
- Get<T>() caches storage-pool pointers rather than calling registry::get<T>(), which routes through assure<T>() -> pools.find(type_hash<T>) (a dense_map probe) on EVERY access. Independently perf-reviewed.
- No view/pool iteration introduced anywhere (ADR Decision 4) - verified by grep.

Honest caveat recorded in ADR Appendix A: even with pool caching this is an immediate per-access INCREASE (~5-6 dependent loads vs 1; both entt's sparse index and payload are paged), not neutral. The payoff needs real systems iterating pools directly.

won't-fix: invalid premise. principal-engineer analysis confirms the ~7.9 ExecuteActiveQueries-calls/turn figure is an artifact of TurnManager's fast-forward loop under autostart-speed=20 (7-8 distinct simulation turns per rendered frame), not repeated invocations within a single turn -- at normal 1x speed there is exactly one call per turn. Sharing a TaskBatch across turns is also unsafe: ExecuteActiveQueries's worker tasks read/write m_EntityData and query.lastMatch, and PostMessage(RangeUpdate) at the end of each call feeds JS OnRangeUpdate handlers (UnitAI/BuildingAI/Auras/Gate/TriggerPoint) whose effects are visible before the same turn's MotionFormation/MotionUnit/Final phases and before the next turn -- deferring flush+Get across turns would race and break determinism/replay. Additionally numFutures already == workerCount in practice, so PushTasks already takes the single notify_all path per call (bd_0ad-92h captured the full available win here). Remaining wake-latency cost is already tracked as bd_0ad-jto (spin-then-sleep workers), which is the correct, determinism-neutral place to pursue further gains.
